title: Long furulya
summary: The long furulya is a Hungarian duct flute, two or three times longer than the six-hole folk flute and usually with five finger holes. A wooden beak sends the air onto an edge, and the long tube gives low, soft tones; burnt rings mark the wood.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. Six notes of the five-note mode are lit down the tube.
Each strike shows the fingering of that note and a band of breath runs from the beak to it.
Let the long notes swell slowly before the next.
rules: A phrase is a line of notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It belongs to the repertoire of shepherds, who play its slow, soft tunes in the open country.
credits: Tradition: the long furulya; tunes written for this game
